items.title: Amazon Aurora DSQL now supports multi-Region peering across continents
items.content_snippet: Amazon Aurora DSQL now lets you create multi-Region clusters whose Regions are on different continents, such as US East (N. Virginia) and Europe (Ireland). Until now, the Regions in a multi-Region cluster had to be in the same geographic Region set. With intercontinental multi-Region clusters, applications on two continents read and write to one strongly consistent database. items.title: AWS Marketplace now supports buyer contact sharing at subscription
items.content_snippet: AWS Marketplace now supports buyer contact sharing. When customers subscribe to a third-party product, they can share their contact information with the seller. This helps sellers onboard new customers, send deployment guides and setup instructions, provide technical support, and share product updates from the start of the subscription. items.title: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store raises API throughput limits
items.content_snippet: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store has increased the default throughput limits for five API operations. items.title: AWS Transform supports optimized storage for server migration
items.content_snippet: AWS Transform for migrations now recommends the optimized storage type and configuration for every server you migrate, so you no longer do it server by server. Building on recent storage assessment capabilities , AWS Transform's recommendations use each server's observed performance and capacity data to reduce overprovisioning costs and avoid performance issues after cutover. items.title: AWS Marketplace now supports buyer approval workflows
items.content_snippet: Today, AWS Marketplace announces the general availability of buyer approvals. This lets you decide which AWS Marketplace purchases need sign-off, who approves them, and where approval happens. You can define buying policies for the conditions that matter to you, such as purchase amount, product type, pricing, and whether an offer is public or private. items.title: Amazon Connect Customer enables Cases by default for new instances
items.content_snippet: Amazon Connect Customer enables Cases by default for new instances, so operations teams can start tracking and resolving customer issues on day one without any setup work. New instances come with Cases connected to rules for setting SLAs, Customer Profiles for personalizing customer experiences, and Amazon EventBridge for triggering actions in other business applications when a case is updated. items.title: AWS Transform automates source and migration target actions to accelerate cutover
items.content_snippet: AWS Transform now automates the tasks that prepare and validate your servers during a migration, before they move and after they launch on AWS. AWS Transform is the agentic AI service that speeds up cloud migration, application modernization, and continuous tech debt reduction. items.title: Amazon OpenSearch Memory is now generally available
items.content_snippet: Today, AWS announced the general availability of Amazon OpenSearch Memory, a new serverless capability in Amazon OpenSearch Service for adding persistent memory to AI agents. OpenSearch Memory stores agent interactions as searchable events, derives useful memories, and retrieves relevant context across sessions, so agents can recall prior decisions, earlier interactions, and user preferences without replaying the full conversation history to the model. items.title: Introducing the Apache Spark Optimization Agent for AWS Glue ETL
items.content_snippet: AWS Glue ETL now offers the Apache Spark Optimization Agent, which analyzes completed Spark job runs and delivers cost and performance optimization recommendations within minutes. You can select a cost or performance goal, and the agent returns specific configuration changes with the telemetry evidence and reasoning behind each suggestion. items.title: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports cross-Region inference routing
items.content_snippet: Today, Amazon SageMaker AI announces cross-Region inference routing, which helps keep inference applications available when a region runs short of capacity by sending requests to endpoints deployed in other AWS Regions and AWS accounts. Models served on accelerated instances can reach capacity limits in a single Region, and an unhealthy endpoint can lead to throttling and errors for end users. items.title: AWS Lambda now supports GPU instances for Event Functions on Lambda Managed Instances
items.content_snippet: GPU support is now available for EC2 G-series GPU instances for Event Functions running on AWS Lambda Managed Instances (LMI). items.title: Introducing ChatGPT for Accounting
items.content_snippet: ChatGPT for Accounting helps take the busywork out of your month-end close. Watch how ChatGPT finds completed jobs in your email and drafts QuickBooks invoices for your review, flagging anything unclear along the way. The Accounting plugin also helps you reconcile transactions, process invoices and receipts, and prepare monthly reports using your existing spreadsheets and connected accounting tools. Learn more about the plugins: https://openai.com/business/solutions/accounting

items.title: What it takes to set intelligence free — Fabian Hedin, CTO, Lovable
items.content_snippet: Lovable nearly failed after building a sophisticated multi agent framework, Fabian Hedin says. At CODE Summit 2026, its CTO explains what changed: durable agent runtimes, Git inspired histories and forkable computers that support long running coding agents. Sandbox checkpointing, copy on write memory, a Rust rewrite of Vite and verification feedback loops connect reliable software generation to product and business outcomes. Speaker info: - https://x.com/FabianHedin - https://www.linkedin.com/in

items.title: Post-Training Gemini 4 for Real Engineering Work — Melvin Johnson, Google DeepMind
items.content_snippet: Passing the tests does not mean a coding agent solved the problem. At CODE Summit 2026, Google DeepMind's Melvin Johnson explains Gemini 4 post training for real engineering work, from harder tasks and rubric based grading to isolated evaluation environments. He connects reinforcement learning, reward hacking, honest model behavior and feedback from Google's engineers to faster releases, alongside Gemini 4 Carbon and Hydrogen. Speaker info: - https://melvin.app/ - https://research.google/people/
